title: Confessions
author: Saint Augustine
description: Augustine’s account of his own life, written around 400. The turning point comes in Milan: a crisis in a garden in 386, then baptism by the city’s bishop, Ambrose, at Easter 387. Ambrose lies in the crypt of Sant’Ambrogio, the brick church he founded.

title: Leonardo and the Last Supper
author: Ross King
description: Art historian Ross King on how Leonardo da Vinci painted the Last Supper in the 1490s for Duke Ludovico Sforza, while war closed in on Milan. It is short and clear. The mural is still on the dining-hall wall of the Santa Maria delle Grazie convent.

title: The Betrothed
author: Alessandro Manzoni
place: Casa del Manzoni museum, Via Morone
description: Italy’s great 19th-century novel: two village lovers kept apart by a local lord, with bread riots and the plague of 1630 in Milan. It’s long. Alessandro Manzoni lived and died in the house on Via Morone, now a museum of his life.

title: Calcio: A History of Italian Football
author: John Foot
description: Historian John Foot on Italian football: the clubs, the fans, the scandals and the money. Milan has two of the biggest clubs, AC Milan and Inter. They share one ground, the San Siro stadium, which opened in 1926 and holds about 75,000.

title: The Body of Il Duce
author: Sergio Luzzatto
description: Historian Sergio Luzzatto follows Benito Mussolini’s corpse after partisans shot him in April 1945. It was hung upside down from a petrol station roof on Piazzale Loreto, now a busy traffic square, then buried, stolen and fought over for years.

title: Poem Strip
author: Dino Buzzati
place: Corriere della Sera offices, Via Solferino
description: Novelist Dino Buzzati retold the Orpheus myth as a comic book set in 1960s Milan: a pop singer follows his dead lover through a door in a city street into the afterlife. Buzzati spent his working life at the Corriere della Sera newspaper on Via Solferino.

title: Accidental Death of an Anarchist
author: Dario Fo
description: A farce by Nobel-winning playwright Dario Fo. In December 1969 anarchist Giuseppe Pinelli fell to his death from a window of Milan’s police headquarters, held after the Piazza Fontana bank bombing that killed 17. Fo mocks the official story.

title: The Sack of Rome
author: Alexander Stille
description: Journalist Alexander Stille on Silvio Berlusconi, the Milan builder who made a TV fortune, owned AC Milan and became prime minister. It covers the 1990s Clean Hands bribery inquiry, run from the Palace of Justice, the city’s vast 1930s courthouse.

title: The House of Gucci
author: Sara Gay Forden
description: Fashion journalist Sara Gay Forden on how a Florentine leather firm became a global brand and a family war. In 1995 Maurizio Gucci was shot dead on the steps of his office at Via Palestro 20. His ex-wife, Patrizia Reggiani, was convicted of ordering it.

title: Italian Ways: On and Off the Rails from Milan to Palermo
author: Tim Parks
description: English novelist Tim Parks, who has taught in Milan for years, reads Italy through its trains: ticket rules, commuters, strikes and the new fast lines. Much of it starts at Milano Centrale, the vast stone station finished under Mussolini in 1931.
